PROVISION OF RURAL EMPLOYMENT AFTER LOCKDOWN 
 
622  SHRI HARNATH SINGH YADAV: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether action has been taken by Government to provide employment opportunities 
to the youth of the rural areas of the country, particularly after lockdown due to 
COVID-19pandemic; and 
(b)  if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR) 
 
 
(a)&(b): The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (Mahatma 
Gandhi NREGS), is a demand driven wage employment programme. A rural household, adult 
members of which agree to unskilled manual work, is entitled for hundred days of wage employment. 
During the current financial year 2020-21 (so far), more than 1.6 crore new job cards have been 
issued. Total number of person worked during the current FY 2020-21 (so far) is 10.28 crore which is 
30% more than that of the FY 2019-20. The Government enhanced the allocation under Mahatma 
Gandhi NREGA for the Financial Year 2020-21 from BE Rs.61,500 crore to Rs.1,11,500 crore and 
more than 324 crore persondays have been generated so far under Mahatma Gandhi NREGA. 
  
Government of India has launched Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (GKRA) of 125 days on 
20
th June, 2020 to boost employment and livelihood opportunities for returnee migrant workers and 
similarly affected citizens in rural area, in the wake of COVID-19 pandemic. The objectives of the 
Abhiyaan were to provide immediate employment & livelihood opportunities to the distressed, to 
saturate the villages with public infrastructure and creation of livelihood assets to boost the income 
generation activities and enhance long term livelihood opportunities by giving focus on 25 works in 
116 selected districts across 6 States of Bihar, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Rajasthan and 
Uttar Pradesh. A total of 12 Ministries/Departments of Government of India has participated in the 
Abhiyaan. A total of 50.78 Crore Persondays employment has been generated during the Abhiyaan.  
  
Deen Dayal Upadhyay-Grameen Kaushal Yojana (DDU-GKY), of this Ministry is a 
placement linked Skill development programme for wage employment. Under this programme a total 
number of 36933 candidates have been placed in jobs in the current financial year 2020-21 (so far).  
 
Rural Self Employment and Training Institutes (RSETIs) of this Ministry is a skill 
development programme which enable trainees to take bank credit and start his/her own micro 
enterprises. Under this programme a total number of 93874 candidates have been settled in the 
current financial year 2020-21 (so far).

EFFECT OF MGNREGS WAGES ON COST OF CULTIVATION 
 
629  DR. BANDA PRAKASH: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the wages under MGNREGS are going to affect the cost of cultivation; 
(b)  whether any steps have been taken by Government to make the MGNREGS labour 
friendly and also cultivator friendly; 
(c)  if so, the details thereof; and 
(d)  if not, the reasons therefor?  
 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR) 
 
 
 
(a) to (d)    Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005, already lays 
emphasis that at least 60% of works at district level in terms of cost shall be for creation of 
productive assets directly linked to Agriculture and Allied Activities which include works related 
to water security like construction of farm ponds, wells, earthen check dams, field channel and 
other water harvesting structures. Mahatma Gandhi NREGS is providing a fall back option for 
livelihood security to the rural poor and is not a regular employment scheme. The Act provides 
that works which are non-tangible, not measurable and repetitive such as removing grass, 
pebbles, and agricultural operations shall not be taken up.  
 
 There are 262 works which are permissible under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS, of which 
182 kinds of works relate to Natural Resources Management (NRM) and out of the 182 NRM 
works, 85 are water related. 164 of the total works are related to Agriculture and Allied 
Activities works. Further, the Mahatma Gandhi NREG Act has suitable provisions for its 
beneficiaries for unemployment allowance, delay compensation, work site facilities, insurance 
coverage and medical facilities for beneficiaries during the work period.

Learning (RPL). STT is being imparted to school/college dropouts/ unemployed youth at 
accredited and affiliated Training Centres (TCs). Under RPL, individuals with prior learning 
experience or skills are assessed and certified. It aims to align the competencies of the 
unregulated workforce of the country to the National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF).

implemented through five types of projects namely RPL Camps, RPL at Employer’s Premises, 
RPL centres, Best-in-Class Employer and Demand Aggregator Portal. RPL in Camp mode is 
suitable where a certain group / cluster of candidates with particular skill sets are 
concentrated. These candidates are provided with a mandatory orientation of 12 hours. Under 
RPL Camps, as on 02.02.2021, 22,86,610 candidates have been oriented across the country 
including 39,717 candidates in State of Haryana and 2,79,342 Candidates in State of Uttar 
Pradesh.

candidates with an outlay of Rs. 948.90 Cr. PMKVY 3.0 encourages and promotes skill

SKILL DEVELOPMENT FOR TRIBALS 
 
635      SHRI BHASKAR RAO NEKKANTI:  
Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased 
to state: 
 
(a) whether any skilling initiatives are being contemplated or implemented specifically for 
tribals, in particular the tribals of Odisha who constitute 22.13 percent of the State’s 
population; 
 
(b)  if so, the details thereof ; and  
 
(c)  if not, the reasons therefor?  
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF  
SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP  
(SHRI R.K. SINGH)  
 
(a) to (c): The Government has adopted a multi-pronged strategy for the overall development of 
tribal people living across the country including Odisha, which includes supports for skill training. 
The Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana  2016-20 (PMKVY 2016-20) and Jan Shikshan 
Sansthan (JSS) Scheme being implemented by the Ministry of Skill Development and 
Entrepreneurship provides short term training to the youths including tribal youths through 
affiliated Training Partners/ Training Centres (TCs). Under PMKVY, 13,209 TCs including 350 
TCs in Odisha and 723 Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Kendras  (PMKKs) including 28 PMKKs in 
Odisha have been empanelled for imparting training. 26,000 Scheduled Tribe (ST) candidates 
have been trained, of which 17,914 candidates have been certified and more than 4,000 
candidates reported placed till 17
th January, 2021. Under JSS, since 2018-19, a total number of 
12,129 ST persons have been trained in Odisha till 31st January, 2021.   
 
So far as long-term skilling is concerned, 23 percent of seats in the Industrial Training 
Institutes (ITIs) are reserved for ST candidates in Odisha by the State Government. Besides, 23 
percent of seats are also reserved for apprenticeship training for ITI pass-out ST candidates in 
the State. All ST candidates whose parental income is less than Rs. 2.50 lakhs per annum are 
exempt from payment of admission fee. ST candidates are also reimbursed Rs. 3000/- towards 
ITI Uniforms. So far as admission of tribal students in Odisha is concerned, 3,571 tribal students 
have taken admission in 49 Government ITIs out of 17,545 total admissions in 2020-21, which is 
20.35 percent of the total admission. The Ministry of Tribal Affairs, the nodal Ministry in the 
Government of India, for overall policy, planning and coordination of programmes for 
development of STs, provides funding support to States for vocational trainings to tribals under 
the Special Central Assistance to Tribal Sub-Scheme (SCA to TSS). Odisha has been given Rs. 
136 crores under this scheme from 2016-17 to 2019-20.

637. SHRI SYED NASIR HUSSAIN:   SMT. PHULO DEVI NETAM: 
SHRI RAJMANI PATEL:    DR. L. HANUMANTHAIAH:          
 
Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be 
pleased to state:
 
  
(a)       whether Government has successfully trained 1 crore youth, as targeted, on 
the completion of the second phase of PMKVY in 2020;  
 
(b)       if so, the details thereof including the number of trained persons; 
 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor ; 
 
(d) the number of trainees who have received employment after their training 
under PMKVY 2.0; 
 
(e) whether an analysis to understand the reasons for the non-employment of 
trainees has been done and a review of the existing training programmes conducted ; 
and 
 
(f) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF  
SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
(SHRI R. K. SINGH) 
 
(a) to (c)          Yes Sir. Under PMKVY (2016-20), as on 19.01.2021, 46.27 lakh 
candidates have been trained under short term training (STT) and 60.68 lakh 
candidates have been oriented under Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) across the 
country.
 
  
(d)       Under the scheme, placement opportunities are being provided to candidates 
certified under STT. RPL does not mandate placement as it orients and certifies 
candidates with prior learning experience or skills. Under PMKVY (2016-20), as on 
19.01.2021, 46.27 lakh and 36.04 lakh candidates have been trained and certified, 
respectively, under Short Term Training (STT) courses. Out of these certified 
candidates, 18.95 lakh candidates have been provided with placement.
 
  
(e) and (f)       In this regard ,NITI Aayog has done the quick assessment study of the 
scheme. Also, NITI Aayog has conducted an independent evaluation of Centrally 
Sponsored Schemes including PMKVY (2016-20). The report of NITI Aayog 
highlighted the mismatch between industry requirement and candidate expectation.  
 
357

  
In addition, National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), an implementing 
agency of PMKVY (2016-20), has also engaged a third party agency, Sambodhi 
Research and Communications Pvt. Ltd., for the impact evaluation of Pradhan Mantri 
Kaushal Vikas Yojana 2016-20. This report highlighted about 15% increase in 
average monthly salary under STT and 19% under RPL. Under RPL, 70% 
participants reported for better chance of finding employment. This report also 
suggested for stronger role of State Skill Development Mission (SSDM) for better 
implementation of scheme. 
 
 
            Based on the above said studies and learning from the implementation of 
PMKVY 1.0 and 2.0, Ministry has launched the new and modified version of PMKVY 
i.e. PMKVY 3.0 (2020-21) on 15.01.2021 with a demand-driven and bottom-up 
approach. The greater roles of State/ SSDM have been provisioned. Under the 
scheme, informed choice / aspirations of the candidates have been given primacy 
and supports candidates to opt for local skills with local jobs.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
 
RAJYA SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 640 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 05.02.2021 
  
SKILL DEVELOPMENT CENTRES 
 
640.  DR. VIKAS MAHATME: 
 
Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to 
state: 
  
(a)       the number of persons trained in various skill development centres from 2016 to this day, 
State/UT-wise;  
 
(b)       the number of people provided employment after getting training from skill development 
and entrepreneurship training centres during the said period, State-wise; and 
 
(c) the target fixed for providing employment to those who have not been provided 
employment so far despite being trained; and 
 
(d) the special steps being taken by Government in order to achieve targets in hilly, backward, 
inaccessible tribal and remote areas? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF  
SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
(SHRI R. K. SINGH) 
 
(a) Under Skill India Mission, Ministry is implementing its flagship scheme Pradhan Mantri 
Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) to impart skill development training to prospective youth of the 
country through short term training (STT) courses in accredited and affiliated training centres 
(TCs) and Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL). Under PMKVY 2.0 (2016-20), as on 19.01.2021, 
46.27 lakh candidates have been trained under STT in around 15,124 TCs and 60.68 lakh 
candidates have been oriented under RPL. The State-wise number of candidates trained / 
oriented under PMKVY (2016-20), as on 19.01.2021, is given at column (c) of Annexure. 
 
(b) Under placement linked Short Term Training (STT) component of PMKVY (2016-20), as 
on 19.01.2021, 36.04 lakh candidates have been certified; out of which, 18.95 lakh candidates 
have been placed. The State-wise number of placed candidates under STT - PMKVY (2016-20) 
is given at column (a) of Annexure. 
 
(c) Under PMKVY, no such targets have been fixed for providing employment to those who 
have not been provided employment so far despite being trained. However, under the scheme, 
various initiatives are taken to enhance placement of the certified candidates such as 
organization of Rozgar Melas with the support of Sector Skill Councils; placement linked release 
of last tranche to the Training Centres (TCs); post 12 months of trainee retention on employment, 
TCs are incentivized @ Rs. 3000 per trainee; post placement support of Rs. 1500 per month per 
364

trainee is applicable for special areas/special groups;  one time placement travel cost upto 
maximum of Rs. 4,500/- per candidate; implementation of employer led training model; 
reallocation of target to TCs based on placement performance, TCs / Training Providers (TPs) 
are required to have dedicated mentorship-cum-placement cells for industry linkage and 
placement of candidates, etc.  
 
(d) Under PMKVY 2016-20, in order to encourage and assist training in Special Areas such as 
hilly, backward, inaccessible tribal and remote areas, the following special provisions have been 
provided, such as: 
 
i. Additional amount equal to 10% of the Base Cost is permitted for Skill Development 
programmes conducted in ‘Special Areas’. 
ii. Complete Boarding and lodging pay-out is provided to candidates undergoing trainings 
outside of Special Areas. 
iii. Transport costs: Candidates from Special Areas undergoing training outside these Special 
Areas, to and fro transport cost as per actual and scheme guidelines. 
iv. Post placement support of Rs. 1500 per month per trainee is applicable for special group 
(women candidates and persons with disability) and special areas (LWE, North East region 
and J&K) for 2 or 3 month post training depending on placement within or outside the district 
of the domicile of the candidate. 
v. Relaxations for setting up training centre to Training providers- 
• Minimum carpet area of 1500 sq. ft. permissible for training centres in North-Eastern 
States. 
• Walls and roof made of Tin / Bamboo sheets allowed for centres in North East.   
• Availability of AC in High-altitude Regions (Above 5000 ft above sea level), is 
exempted.

 क्या रसायन और उववरक  मंत्री यह बताने की क ृपा करेंगे कक :

(क) और (ख ): कोववड -19 महामारी के मद्देनजर , प्रिानमंत्री भारतीय जन औषधि पररयोजना (पीएमबीजेपी) 
ने राष्ट्र के ललए आवचयक सेवाएं प्रदान की हैं। सभी प्रिानमंत्री भारतीय जनऔषधि क ें द्रों (पीएमबीजेके) ने 
ननयलमत रूप से अपने संचालन को बनाए रखा और नागररकों को दवा इयां उपलब्ि कराई। सभी ववननमााण 
इकाइयां जो पीएमबीजेके  के ललए दवाइयां/सश्जाकल की आप ूनता कर रही  थीं, को स्वास््य और पररवार 
कल्याण मंत्रालय और राज्य/स्थानीय प्रशासन के ननदेशों/ददशाननद ेशों के अन ुसार सभी कोववड  संबंधित स ुरिा 
प्रोटोकॉल का पालन करने का ननद ेश ददया गया था। इसके अनतररक्त , भारतीय फामाा पीएसय ू ब्यूरो 
(बीपीपीआई) के गोदामों (वेयरहाउसों) में दवाइयों की प्राश्तत के समय , आवक स्टॉक का ननयलमत  रूप से 
स्वच्छीकरण (सैनेटाइज) ककया जाता था। साथ ही , स्टोरों पर सभी कोववड  संबंधित स ुरिा प्रोटोकॉल का 
पालन ककया जाता था। यह स ुननश्चचत ककया गया था कक सख्त लॉकडाउन उपायों के बावज ूद , पीएमबीजेके 
को ननयलमत रूप से दवाइयों की आप ूनता जारी रखी जाए।

उपभोक्ता मामले नर्भाग 
 
राज्य सभा 
अतारा ांकित प्रश्न सांख्या 561   
 
किसिा उत्तर शुक्रवार 5 फरवरी, 2021  िो किया िाएगा  
 
 कििी ि ांपकियों द्वारा खाद्यान्िों िा भांडारण  
561 #  श्री छ. उियिरािे भोंसले: 
 चौधरी सु
खराम कस ांह यािव:  
 श्री कवशम्भर प्रसाि किषाि: 
 श्रीमती छाया वमाा: 
क्या उपभोक्ता मामले, खाद्य और सावािकिि कवतरण मांत्री यह बतािे की कृ पा करेंगे नक: 
(क) आर्श्यक र्स्त ु (सं
शोधि) अनधनियम, 2020 क े  अिुसार निजी कं पनियों क े  नलए खाद्यान्ि भंडारण की 
अिुमेय सीमा नकतिी है; 
(ख) क्या सरकार इस सीमा पर स्टॉक नियं
त्रण लगािे पर नर्चार कर रही है;  
(ग) यनि कनतपय कं पनियां
 इस अनधनियम क े  आधार पर िेश क े  खाद्यान्िों को खरीि लें और जरूरत पड़िे पर 
जारी ि करें, तो इस नस्िनत में सरकार क े  समक्ष कािूिी नर्कल्प क्या है; और 
(घ) तत्सं
बं
धी ब्यौरा क्या है? 
 
उत्तर 
उपभोक्ता मामले, खाद्य और सावािकिि कवतरण राज्य मांत्री 
(श्री िािवे रावसाहेब िािाराव)  
 
(क) और (ख): खाद्यान्िों क े  भंडारण की अिुमेय सीमा क े  सं
बं
ध में कोई अनधसूचिा क े र्ल तभी जारी की जाती 
है, जब आर्श्यक र्स्त ु अनधनियम क े  तहत खाद्यान्िों पर स्टॉक सीमा लगाई जाती है। आर्श्यक र्स्तु (सं
शोधि) 
अनधनियम, 2020 में यह प्रार्धाि है नक स्टॉक सीमा लगािे की कोई भी कारवर्ाई म ूल्य र् ृनि अिावत् तत्काल 
पूर्वर्ती बारह माह की प्रचनलत कीमत, या नर्गत पा ं
च र्र्षों की औसत खुिरा कीमत, जो भी कम हो, की त ुलिा 
में (i) बागर्ािी उत्पाि क े  खुिरा मूल्य में सौ प्रनतशत र्ृनि; या (ii) शीघ्र िष्ट ि होिे र्ाले कृ नर्ष खाद्य पिािों क े  
खुिरा मूल्य में पचास प्रनतशत र्ृनि; पर आधाररत होगी। स ंशोधि में यह प्रार्धाि है नक ऐसे आिेश नकसी कृ नर्ष 
उत्पाि क े  नकसी प्रोसेसर या मूल्य श्ृंखला प्रनतभागी पर लागू िहहो होंगे, यनि ऐसे क्यनक्त की स्टॉक सीमा प्रसं
स्करण 
क े  नलए सं
स्िानपत क्षमता की समग्र सीमा या नियावतक क े  मामले में नियावत की मां
ग से अनधक िहहो है। 
 
(ग) और (घ): राज्य सरकारों क े  साि-साि क ें द्रीय सरकार, चोरबाजारी निर्ारण और आर्श्यक र्स्तु प्रिाय 
अनधनियम, 1980, नजसमें चोरबाजारी की रोकिाम और आर्श्यक र्स्त ुओं की आपूनतव बिाए रखिे क े  नलए ऐसे 
मामलों में नगरफ्तारी का प्रार्धाि है, क े  तहत अपिी शनक्तयों का उपयोग करिा जारी रखेगी।

(पीएमएफएमई) योिना क े  तहत ओदिशा राज्य ने नबरंगपुर दिले क े  दलए मक्का आिाररत उत्पािों को 
एक दिला एक उत्पाि (ओिीओपी) क े  रूप में चुना है दिसे मंत्रालय ने अनुमोदित दकया है। आत्म दनभभर 
भारत अदभयान क े  तहत खाद्य प्रसंस्करण उद्योग मंत्रालय ने मौिूिा सूक्ष्म खाद्य प्रसंस्करण उद्यमों क े  
उन्नयन क े  दलए दवत्तीय, तकनीकी और व्यावसादयक सहायता प्रिान करने क े  दलए क ें द्र प्रायोदित योिना 
पीएमएफएमई शुरू की है।  
इस योिना का उद्देश्य सूक्ष्म खाद्य प्रसंस्करण उद्यमों की प्रदतस्पिाभत्मकता को प्रोत्साहन िेना और मौिूिा 
खाद्य प्रसंस्करण यूदनटों, दकसान उत्पािक संगठनों, स्वयं सहायता समूहों, उत्पािक सहकारी सदमदतयों 
और सहकारी सदमदतयों को ऋण दलंक्ि अनुिान और क्षमता दनमाभण क े  माध्यम से अपनी संपूणभ मूल्य 
श्ृंखला क े  सार्थ समर्थभन िेना है। इस योिना में सामानय अवसंरचना, दवपणन और ब्ांदिंग क े  दलए समर्थभन 
िेने की भी पररकल्पना की गई है। 
यह योिना इनपुटों की खरीि , सामान्य सेवाओं का लाभ उठाने और उत्पािों क े  दवपणन क े  संिभभ में 
पैमाने का लाभ उठाने क े  दलए ओिीओपी दृदिकोण अपनाती  है। ओिीओपी दृदिकोण मूल्य श्ृंखला 
दवकास और समर्थभन अवसंरचना क े  संरेखण क े  दलए ढांचा प्रिान करेगा। ओिीओपी उत्पािों क े  दलए 
नई यूदनटों का भी समर्थभन दकया िाएगा।

सांलग् नि-II  
 
मेगा फ ू ड पाि योजना ि े  बारे में राज् य सभा में किनाांि 05.02.2021 िो पूछ े  जाने वाले 
अताराांकित प्रश् न सां 574  ि े  भाग (ग) ि े  उत् तर में उल्लिल्लखत कववरण ।  
 
मेगा फ ू ड पाि थ िीम किशाकनिेशोां ि े  मुख् य लक्षण ।  
थ िीम ि े  उद्देश् य:  
 मेगा फ ू ड पाक त  स् कीम का प्राथदमक उद्देश् य खेत से लेकर बाजार तक मूल् य श्ृंखला सदहत खाद्य 
प्रसंस् करण क े  दलए आधुदनक अवसंरचना सुदवधाए ं  उपलब् ध कराना है । इसमें , खेत से नजिीक 
प्रसंस् करण अवसंरचना का सृजन, पररवहन, लॉदजस्स्टक् स तथा क ें द्रीयक ृ त प्रसंस् करण क ें द्र शादमल   होंगे 
।  
 स् कीम, मेगा फ ू ड पाकों की स् थापना द्वारा हब एवं स् पॉक माडल आधाररत क् लस् टर दृदिकोण पर 
कायत करती है । इसमें , प्राथदमक प्रसंस् करण क ें द्रों (पीपीसीज) क े  रूप में खेत क े  नजिीक प्राथदमक 
प्रसंस् करण एवं भंडारण क े  दलए अवसंरचना का सृजन और क ें द्रीय प्रसंस् करण क ें द्र में संग्रहण क ें द्र 
(सीसीज), सामान् य सुदवधाए ं  त था सडक, दबजली, पानी तथा अपदशष् ट  उपचार संयंत्र (ईटीपी) सुदवधाए ं  
आदि जैसी समथतकारी अवसंरचना शादमल हैं । ये पीपीसीज और सीसीज, सीपीसी में अवस्स्थत प्रसंस् करण 
यूदनटों क े  दलए कच् ची सामग्री की आपूदतत करने हेतु एकत्रीकरण और भंडारण क ें द्रों क े  रूप में कायत 
करती हैं ।  यह स् की म मांग प्रेररत होगी और यह खाद्य प्रसंस् करण यूदनटों को पयातवरणीय एवं संरक्षा 
मानकों को पूरा करने में सहायता करेगी ।  
सहायता िा पैटनक:  
 स् कीम क े  अंतगतत सामान् य क्षेत्रों में पररयोजना लागत (भूदम लागत को छोडकर) क े  50% की िर 
से और िुगतम तथा पहाडी क्षेत्रों अथातत दसस्िम , जम् मू और कश् मीर, दहमाचल प्रिेश, उत् त राखंड तथा 
राज् यों क े  आईटीडीपी अदधसूदचत क्षेत्रों सदहत पूवोत् तर क्षेत्र में पररयोजना लागत (भूदम लागत को छोडकर) 
क े  75% की िर से परंतु प्रदत पररयोजना अदधकतम 50 करोड रुपए का पूंजी अनुिान दिया जाता है ।  
भूकम:  
 मेगा फ ू ड पाक त  क े  क ें द्रीय प्रसंस् करण क ें द्र क े  दलए सीपीसी की स् थापना हेतु या तो खरीि अथवा 
कम से कम 75 वषों की पट्टे पर न् यूनतम 50 एकड भूदम अपेदक्षत होती है ।  
मुख् य पररयोजना घटि:  
 समथकिारी मूल अवसांरचना- अंिर की सडक ें, जल दनकासी, जल आपूदतत , क ै दिव पॉवर

 िोर प्रसांथ िरण - छ ं टाई एवं वगीकरण, पैक े दजंग, मालगोिाम एवं दवदशष् टीक ृ त भंडारण, 
प्री-क ू दलंग एवं पक् वन चैम् बसत, आईक् यूएफ, शीत श्ृखला अवसंरचना , वाष् प सृजन , क् यूसी 
प्रयोगशाला आदि ।  
 सूक्ष् म एवां लघु उद्यमोां (एमएसईज) ि े  कलए थ टैंडडक कडजाइन फ ै सीकलटी शेड्स - छोटी

 मेगा फ ू ड पाक त  क े  दनष् पािन, स् वादमत् व एवं प्रबंधन की दजम् मेिारी क ं पनी अदधदनयम क े  अंतगतत

एसपीवी ि े  कलए पात्रता मानिांड:  
एसवीपी क े  मुख् य पात्रता मानिंड दनम् नानुसार हैं:-  
i. एसपीवी क ं पनी अदधदनयम क े  तहत एक पंजीक ृ त कारपोरेट दनकाय होगी । तथादप , 
पररयेाजना का कायातन् व यन कर रही राज् य  सरकार/राज् य सरकार की 
इकाइयों/सहकाररताओं क े  मामले में क ं पनी अदधदनयम क े  तहत एक अलग एसपीवी का

ii. एसपीवी में अदधकतम इस्िटी धारण करने वाला प्रमोटर प्रमुख प्रमोटर होगा । प्रमुख प्रमोटर 
खाद्य प्रसंस् करण उद्योग मंत्रालय सदहत दहतधारकों क े  साथ समन् वय करने क े  दलए प्राथदमक 
रूप से दजम् मेिार होगा तादक पररयोजना का प्रभावी कायातन् वयन सुदनदित हो सक े  ।  
iii. प्रमोटर/एसपीवी क े  प्रस् तादवत शेयर धारकों की समेदकत दनवल पूंजी 50.00 करोड रुपए से 
कम नहीं होगी । एसपीवी में प्रत् येक सिस् य क े  पास उसक े  प्रस् तादवत इस्िटी अंशिान की 
कम से कम 1.5 गुणा दनवल पूंजी होनी चादहए तादक प्रत् येक शेयर धारक से पररयोजना क े  
दलए अपेदक्षत अंशिान सुदनदित हो सक े  ।  
iv. एसपीवी क े  दलए सामान् य क्षेत्रों में इस्िटी क े  रूप में क ु ल पररयोजना लागत का कम से कम

उत् त राखंड तथा राज् यों क े  आईटीडीपी अदधसूदचत क्षेत्रों पूवोत् त र क्षेत्रों में क ु ल पररयोजना

v. एसपीवी की शेयरधारक बनने वाली क ें द्रीय सरकार की एजेंदसयां एसपीवी में क े वल 26

के प्रावधानों के कायाथन्वयन की समीक्षा राज्यों के सार् समीक्षा बैठकों में अध्ययन और चचाथ के माध्यम

अंतररत ककए गए है, जो ववभभन्न राज्यों में अलग-अलग होते हैं। पंचायतों के  कायथ ननष्पािन की ननगरानी 
राज्य सरकारों द्वारा की जाती है। पंचायती राज मंत्रालय ग्रामीण प्रशासन के भलए पंचायतों के क्षमता 
ननमाथण में राज्यों की सहायता करता है। यह पंचायतों द्वारा  सहभागी योजना बनाने और ग्रा म पंचायत 
ववकास योजनाएं बनाने के  भलए दिशाननिेश तैयार करने में, ववकास के उद्िेश्यों को प्राप्त करने के भलए 
िक्षता, पारिभशथता और जवाबिेही लाने में भी सहायता करता है। आगे, ग्रामीण भारत को सशक्त बनाने के

Need to address the problems of sugarcane farmers in Tamil Nadu 
SHRI P. WILSON (Tami l Nadu): Mr. Chairman, Sir, in Tamil Nadu, the sugarcane 
growers are put to untold h ardships and are in huge financial distress. The sugarcane 
growers sell their produce to about 44 sugar mill factories in Tamil Nadu and 
Puducherry. However, for the past t wo years, the private and public sector sugar 
mills, cooperative sugar mills, includ ing the State Government Cooperative Societies 
have not paid the purchase price of sugarcane to the cane producers and about 
Rs.1,000 crores are due to the sugarcane grower s by these sugar mills. Sadly, more 
than 15 sugar mill factories in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry have been closed, including 
the Government-run Puducherry sugar mill.  These closed mills owe several hundred 
crores of rupees to the sugar cane growers leaving b ehind more than one lakh 
farmers in distress as they have not settled their sugar cane purchase money. 
 Due to closure of sugar mills, more than one lakh workers employed, directly 
or indirectly, are left in lurch and they have not been paid salary for mor e than two to 
three years.   
 Also due to Corona lockdown, there were shortages in la bour to harvest the 
crops.  Thousands of sugar cane growers in Cuddalore, Nagapattinam and Thanjavur 
districts are in huge debts and have mortgaged their lands, sold all t heir jewels, 
drained their savings and virtually standing on streets. 
 The farmers ar e not in a position to recover their sale proceeds from these 
closed mills as nationalised banks have priority over these debts and they have 
invoked the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) by initiating insolvency 
proceedings.  The National Cooperative S ugar Mill has not paid State Advisory Price 
on sugar cane for a period of two years.   
 Besides, nationalised banks are hesitating to give crop loans to these farmers.  
The deadlock in the sugar industry can be set right only when the Central Government 
announces Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) for the sugar season taking into 
consideration the interests of all sections. 
 The Union Government should also come out with a d efinite sugar cane policy 
and should frame a rehabilitation package specifically for sugar cane growers in Tamil 
Nadu, taking into account the pandemic crisis, and sanction a special fund of Rs. 
1000 crores, to be paid, through the nationalised banks, to all the sugar cane growers

THE MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE (SHRI PRAKASH 
JAVADEKAR): (a) to (e) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) to (e) Considering the import ance of the clean air, Government has launched Air 
Quality Index (AQI) in the year 2015. 
Air Quality Index (AQI) provides air pollution status of an area or city but not that 
of any State. AQI of a city depends on multiple factors, which include meteorolo gy, 
geography, local sources such as vehicles, industries, etc. and contribution from 
other regional sources. 
Delhi with higher population, number of vehicles, emission from various other 
local sources as well as contribution of regional sources such as st ubble burning 
(during October, November), dust in summer has higher air pollution levels compared 
to many of the adjoining cities including cities of Punjab.  
With low winds, low temperatures and limited mixing area available for dilution, 
the pollution l evels in Delhi are higher during winter. In October and November, wind 
blows from Punjab towards Delhi. This brings pollution due to stubble burning towards 
Delhi and adds to Delhi’s pollution.  
It is observed that meteorology plays very important role in  air pollution. Other 
metropolitan cities like Chennai, Bengaluru and Mumbai have similar or more pollution 
sources as Delhi. But, air quality in these cities is far better than Delhi due to high 
winds and mixing zone and other meteorological factors.  
With ma ny actions taken by the Government such as introduction of BS -VI, 
expansion of Metro, operationalization of Eastern and Western peripheral 
expressways, shifting of industries to PNG, waste processing plants, online round the 
clock monitoring of red ca tegory industries, etc. Air quality has improved significantly 
in Delhi.  Details are given in the annexure.

THE MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE (SHRI PRAKASH 
JAVADEKAR): (a) and (b) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) and (b) As a result of concerted efforts made for protection and conservation 
of wildlife, the population of several wildlife species like Tigers, Elephants, Asiatic 
Lion, Rhino etc. in the country has increased. There are reports of wild animals 
moving out of the forests leading to human wildlife conflict situations. 
The management of wildlife is primarily the responsibility of the concerned 
States/Union Territories.  
The important steps taken by Government of India to manage and mitigate human -
animal conflict in the country include: 
i.  Funds are provided under the National CAMPA for augmentation of fodder and 
water in forest areas for restricting wild animals to forest areas.  An amount of 
Rs. 47,872.31 crores has been provided to various States for  promoting 
afforestation and achieving green objectives of the country during 2019-2020. 
ii. Ministry provides financial assistance to States/UTs under the Centrally 
Sponsored Schemes of 'Development of Wildlife Habitats', ‘Project Tiger’ and 
‘Project Elep hant’ for  management of wildlife and its habitats in the country. 
The broad activities supported under these schemes include habitat 
enrichment, water augmentation. 
iii. The funds are also used for construction /erection of physical barriers such as 
solar powered electric fence, bio -fencing using cactus, boundary wall, animal 
proof trenches around forest, etc. 
iv. The financial support to the States/UTs also includes a component of 
compensation due to damage by wild animals. 
v.  Voluntary relocation of villa ges from the core area of Tiger Reserves, National 
Parks and Sanctuaries are also being funded under the Centrally Sponsored 
Scheme: ‘Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats’ as proposed by the 
State Governments for avoiding conflict. 

                                                        [8 FEBRUARY, 2021]                                                                47 
 
 
vi. Periodic awar eness ca mpaigns to sensitize, guide and advise the general 
public on man -animal conflict, including dissemination of information through 
various forms of media. 
vii. Directions have been sent to all States/Union Territories for use of 
undergrounding of cab les upto 33 KV of electricity cables in forest areas and 
also maintaining transmission lines to avoid sagging.  
viii. Government of India has issued Standard Operating Procedures 
(SOPs)/guidelines to manage Human -Tiger/Human-Leopard /Human -
Elephant conflict. 
ix. Ministry, in the year 2018, has increased ex -gratia relief under the Centrally 
Sponsored Scheme in case of depredation by wild animals. 
x. Under the revamped operational guidelines of Pradhan Mantri Fasal  Bima 
Yojna (PMFBY), issued by the Government o f Indi a (e ffective from the year 
2020), States can provide add -on coverage for crop loss due to attack by wild 
animals. 
xi. To mitigate human wildlife conflict along linear infrastructures like rail tracks, 
roads/highways and power transmission lines passi ng thr ough the Protected 
Areas and other wildlife rich areas, the Standing Committee of National Board 
for Wildlife has recommended that all linear infrastructure development 
Agencies, should submit animal passage plans based on the guidelines 
prepared by Wildlife Institute of India.  
xii. The Ministry has approved a project for undertaking immuno -contraceptive 
measures for population management of wild animals.

MR. CHAIRMAN: Question No. 70. 
Development of traditional arts 
*70. SHRI BR IJLAL: Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM 
ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
(a)  the details of schemes in place for development of traditional arts of the country;  
(b)  whether any scheme is under consideration to identify and  develop local arts  of 
other States on the lines of ‘One District One Product’ scheme popularly known as 
ODOP being run by Government of Uttar Pradesh; and  
(c)  if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES (SHRI NITIN 
JAIRAM GADKARI): (a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises is implementing a scheme 
titled ‘Scheme of Fund for Traditional Industries (SFURTI)’.  The main objective of the 
SFURTI s cheme is to organize  the traditional industries and artisans into clusters, 
including clusters of traditional arts, to make them competitive and provide long term 
sustainable employment.  
Under the scheme, two types of clusters are set up.  The maximum fin ancial 
assistance provided is Rs.  2.50 crore for a Regular Cluster (up to 500 artisans) and 

                                                        [8 FEBRUARY, 2021]                                                                59 
 
 
Rs. 5.00 crore for a Major Cluster (more than 500 artisans).  The assistance includes 
infrastructure development like setting up of Common Facility Centers, procure ment 
of new machineries, raw materials, along with training, exposure visits, etc. 
Till date, 335 clusters have been approved under the scheme and 82 clusters 
are functional. These clusters inc lude sectors like Khadi, Coir, Handloom, Traditional 
Dress Maki ng, Handicraft, Traditional Arts like – Kalamkari, Dokra art, Bamboo 
products, Food processing including honey, etc.  The list of these clusters is placed 
at Annexure. 
Besides this, Ministry of  Textiles implements schemes 
for development of traditional arts under ‘National Hand icraft Development 
Programme (NHDP)’ that has 7 components namely (i) Ambedkar Hastshilp Vikas 
Yojana (Base Line Survey & Mobilization of artisans), (ii) Design & Technolo gy Up 
gradation, (iii) Human Resource Development, (iv) Direct Benefit to Artisan, (v ) 
Infrastructure and Technology Support, (vi) Research and Development and (vii) 
Marketing Support & Services. In addition, Ministry of Textiles implements 
‘Comprehensive Handicrafts Cluster Development Scheme (CHCDS)’ that has two 
components namely Mega Cluster & Special Projects under Integrated Development 
and Promotion of Handicraft (IDPH). 
Ministry of Tourism under the Swadesh Darshan scheme provides financial 
assistance to the State Govt./UTs/Central Agencies for setting up proje cts as part of 
development of tourism infrastructure in the country.  Craft Haat/Craft Bazaar, Open 
Air Theatre/Amphi theatres, Souvenir Shops are set up under the scheme to help 
development of traditional arts in the country. 
Ministry of Minority Affairs is implementing a scheme titled USTTAD (Upgrading 
the Skills and Training in Traditional Arts/ Crafts for Development) that aims at 
capacity building and upgrading the traditional skills of maste r craftsmen/artisans; 
training of minority youths in various i dentified traditional arts/crafts; develop national 
and international market linkages and preservation of languishing arts/crafts. Hunar  
Haat has been implemented as a component of this scheme wh ich is an effective 
platform wherein opportunity is given to minority artisans/crafts men and culinary 
experts from across the country to showcase and market their finest handicraft and 
exquisitely crafted indigenous products. 23 Hunar  Haats have been organi zed since 
November, 2016 till December 2020 at different places.

MOTION OF THANKS ON THE PRESIDENT’S ADDRESS 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, the House has taken up the discussion on Motion 
of Thanks on the President’s Address, and we have spent around fifteen hours and 
more than fifty hon. Members from different political parties have tak en part in the 
discussion. Now, it is the time for conclusion, and the reply is going to be given by 
the hon. Prime Minister. So, I call upon hon. Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Bhai Modi 
to reply. 
DR. SANTANU SEN (West Bengal): Sir, All India Trinamool Congress is walking out. 
SHRI MD. NADIMUL HAQUE (West Bengal): Sir, we are walking out. 
MR. CHAIRMAN: He has already said it. He is your leader, follow the leader. Thank 
you. 
(At this stage, some hon. Members left the Chamber) 
MR. CHAIRMAN: This is not a matter of joking. If they want to walk out, they have the 
right. Walk out or talk out is the way out, not the wash out or all out. I am happy. 
Now, hon. Prime Minister will reply to Motion of Thanks on the President’s Address.

new confidence to the world full of challenges. The President's address has been a 
guiding principle for 'self -reliant India' and paved the way  to be followed for the 
decade. Honourable Chairman, Sir, today, I rise here among all of you to express my 
gratitude from the bottom of my heart to the honourable President.

gratitude towards all the honourable Members for enriching this debate. It would have

Need for Reduction of GST on Kendu leaves for the State of Odisha 
 
SHRI SUBHASH CHANDRA SINGH (Odisha):  
♣ "Sir, out of the 4.5 crore population 
of Odisha, 10 lakh people are engaged in Kendu leaf sector. A large section of people 
engaged in this sector are poor, Adivasis and Harijans. Most of them belong to the 
Western part of Odisha, and 80 per cent of them are women. Their financial condition 
is very weak. Sir, 18 per cent GST is levied on Kendu leaf.  In Odisha, prior to the 
implementation of GST, there was 5 per cent tax on Kendu leaf. If this tax could be 
brought down to its earlier level, these poor Adiv asi women and poor men who are 
engaged in this sector between the months of March to June and draw their livelihood 
and sustenance from the Kendu leaf, such women folk could be largely benefitted. 
Our hon. Chief Minister of Odisha Sh. Naveen Patnaik has already written twice to the 
Finance Ministry and to the Chairman, GST. Some direction should come from the 
hon. Chairman in this matter. These 10 lakh people are engaged in this sector. Out of 
this 80 per cent are women. They will get benefitted by their earning with the increase 
in the bonus amount and further they would also get the benefit of security. I urge 
upon the hon. Chairman to direct the Central Government to take a decision to sort 
out the major problem of the Kendu leaf workers, and, accordingly, reduce the GST 
on Kendu leaf from 18 per cent to its earlier level of 5 per cent. Namaskar."

Puducherry. However, for the past two years, the private and public sector sugar 
mills, cooperative sugar mills, including the State Government Cooperative Societies 
have not paid the purchase price of sugarcane to the cane producers and about 
Rs.1,000 crores are due to the sugarcane growers by these sugar mills. Sadly more 
than 15 sugar mill factories in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry have been closed, including 
the Government-run Puducherry sugar mill.  These closed mills owe several hundred 
crores of rupees to the sugar cane growers leaving behind more than one lakh 
farmers in distress as they have not settled their sugar cane purchase money. 
 Due to closure of sugar mills, more than one lakh workers employed, directly 
or indirectly, are left in lurch and they have not been paid salary for more than two to 
three years.   
 Also due to Corona lockdown, there were shortages in labour to harvest the 
crops.  Thousands of sugar cane growers in Cuddalore, Nagapattinam and Thanjavur 
districts are in huge debts and have mortgaged their lands , sold all their jewels, 
drained their savings and virtually standing on streets. 
 The farmers are not in a position to recover their sale proceeds from these 
closed mills as nationalised banks have priority over these debts and they have 
invoked the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) by initiating insolvency 
proceedings.  The National Cooperative Sugar Mill has not paid State Advisory Price 
on sugar cane for a period of two years.   
 Besides, nationalised banks are hesitating to give crop loans to these farmers.  
The deadlock in the sugar industry can be set right only when the Central Government 
announces Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) for the sugar season taking into 
consideration the interests of all sections. 
 The Union Government should also come out with a definite sugar cane policy 
and should frame a rehabilitation package specifically for sugar cane growers in Tamil 
Nadu, taking into account the pandemic crisis, and sanction a special fund of Rs. 
1000 crores, to be paid, through the nationalised banks, to all the sugar cane growers 
in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry....

Best practices for maintaining Air Quality Index 
 
*62. SHRI RAJMANI PATEL: Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government is aware that the State of Punjab recorded a moderate Air 
Quality Index (AQI) in September- October 2020 despite 11,000 stubble 
burning cases, whereas Delhi’s AQI was poor during the same period; 
(b) whether Government has identified causes for this difference between the two 
region's AQI; 
(c) if so, the details thereof, and if not, the reasons therefor; 
[8 February, 2021]
27

(d) whether Government has identified good practices of the State Government of 
Punjab to reduce air pollution; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof, and if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE (SHRI PRAKASH 
JAVADEKAR): (a) to (e) A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
 
Statement 
 
(a) to (e) Considering the importance of the clean air, Government has launched Air 
Quality Index (AQI) in the year 2015. 
 
Air Quality Index (AQI) provides air pollution status of an area or city but not that of 
any State. AQI of a city depends on multiple factors, which include meteorology, 
geography, local sources such as vehicles, industries, etc. and contribution from 
other regional sources. 
Delhi with higher population, number of vehicles, emission from various other lo cal 
sources as well as contribution of regional sources such as stubble burning (during 
October, November), dust in summer has higher air pollution levels compared to 
many of the adjoining cities including cities of Punjab.  
 
With low winds, low temperatures and limited mixing area available for dilution, the 
pollution levels in Delhi are higher during winter. In October and November, wind 
blows from Punjab towards Delhi. This brings pollution due to stubble burning towards 
Delhi and adds to Delhi’s pollution.  
 
It is observed that meteorology plays very important role in air pollution. Other 
metropolitan cities like Chennai, Bengaluru and Mumbai have similar or more pollution 
sources as Delhi. But, air quality in these cities is far better than Delhi due to high 
winds and mixing zone and other meteorological factors.  
 
With many actions taken by the Government such as introduction of BS-VI, expansion 
of Metro, operationalization of Eastern and Western peripheral expressways, shifting 
of industries to PNG, waste processing plants, online round the clock monitoring of 
red category industries, etc. Air quality has improved significantly in Delhi.  Details are 
annexed. 
 
28
[RAJYA SABHA]

The ‘Good’, ‘Satisfactory’ and ‘Moderate’ days increased to 182 in 2019 in comparison 
to 108 in 2016 whereas, number of ‘Poor’, ‘Very Poor’ and ‘Severe’ reduced from 246 
in 2016 to 183 in 2019.  
 
Punjab has reported that actions such as mandatory use of Super Straw Management 
System with Combine Harvester, deployment of district level teams to take stric t 
actions against defaulters, putting up biomass power plants, public awareness 
campaigns, etc. were taken. However, the incidences of stubble burning reported in 
2020 (76,590) has increased as compared to last year (52,991 cases). 
 
Annexure 
 
CENTRAL GOVERNMENT INITIATIVES TO COMBAT AIR POLLUTION IN DELHI- 
NCR 
 
1. ACTIONS TO CONTROL VEHICLE POLLUTION 
 
Introduction of BS-IV and BS-VI Fuel and Emission Norms  
 BS IV fuel and vehicle emission norms were introduced in April 2017 in the entire 
country. BS VI fuel was introduced in Delhi from April 2018, in NCR from October 
2019 and in entire country by April 2020. 
 80% reduction in Particulate Matter emissions and 30% reduction in Nitrogen 
Oxides emissions in BS IV heavy duty diesel vehicles compared with BS III norms. 
 Leapfrogging to BS VI norms is likely to reduce 50% Particulate Matter emissions 
and 88.5% Nitrogen Oxide emissions in comparison to BS IV norms. 
Improvement also in other pollutants and type of vehicles.  
 Nearly ₹60,000 Cr were spent on switching over to BS VI fuels. 
 
Eastern and Western Peripheral Expressways (EPE and WPE) 
 EPE and WPE work completed at cost of about ₹17000 Cr and opened for public 
in May 2018 and November 2018, respectively.  
 30000 to 40000 good vehicles not destined for Delhi ar e diverted away from 
national capital due to WPE and EPE. This helps in reduction traffic congestion 
and pollution caused due to non- destined vehicles which earlier used to pass 
through Delhi. 
Implementation of RFID system at all 13 entry points of Delhi 
[8 February, 2021]
29

 RFID (radio -frequency identity) system implemented by South Delhi Municipal 
Corporation (SDMC) for collection of toll and Environment Compensation 
Charges from commercial vehicles entering Delhi. 
 Cost ₹120 Cr for over the period of next five years (Design, Built, Finance, 
Operate and Transfer) basis. 
 Strict enforcement of Environmental Compensation Charges on Delhi -bound 
trucks helps in control on numbers, including enforcement to check and divert all 
non-Delhi bound truck traffic and age limit (as stipulate d by Hon’ble Supreme 
Court). 
Motor Vehicle Act 2019: Increase in penalty for violation of PUC norms 
 With recent amendment in the Motor Vehicle Act and increase in fine from ₹1000/- 
to ₹10000/-for not having PUC certificate, compliance has increased.  Due t o 
this, average number of daily PUC certificates issued has increased from 10,000 -
12,000 to 40000-45000. 
 
 PUC norms compliance and traffic discipline will help in reduction in vehicular 
pollution in Delhi-NCR, which has a major contribution to pollution levels in Delhi-
NCR. 
Installation of Vapour Recovery Systems in more than 3000 petrol pumps in NCR is 
under implementation. 
Delhi Metro Network Augmentation 
 Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) network now covers about 389 Km with 
285 stations, reaching Delhi-Noida-Greater Noida-Ghaziabad in UP and Gurgaon 
to Ballabhgarh in Haryana. It today has over 300 train sets of four, six and eight

Statement

Red Panda was estimated to be 32 in Neora Valley National Park 
and 38 in Singalila National Park in the year 2012.Estimates 
indicate that the numbers of Red Panda after 2012 are on the rise. 
 
Red Panda are foundin the temperate montane forests in the 
eastern Himalayas. In India, Red Pandas are found in States of 
Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, West Bengal and Meghalaya. They 
are arboreal species and depend on bamboo for their survival. 
 
As informed by the Government of West Bengal and Wildlife Crime 
Control Bureau,no case of Red Panda poaching or illegal trade of 
its body parts has been reported in West Bengal.  
Indian Pangolins, also known as scaly ant eaters, live in burrows  
and are found in large numbers in tropical forests as well as open 
land, grasslands an d degraded habitatsthrough out the country

(a) whether Government is aware of the fact that the population of various wild 
species have multiplied during the last few years and that they are posing danger 
by encroaching into agriculture fields and nearby human habitations, near forest

(b) if so, the measures taken by Government to control the human -animal conflict 
in the country? 
 
THE MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE (SHRI PRAKASH 
JAVADEKAR): (a) and (b) A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
  
Statement 
 
46
[RAJYA SABHA]

(a) and (b) As a result of concerted efforts made for protection and 
conservation of wildlife, the population of several wildlife species like Tigers, 
Elephants, Asiatic Lion, Rhino etc. in the country has increased. There are 
reports of wild animals moving out of the forests leading to human wildlife 
conflict situations. 
 
The management of wildlife is primarily the responsibility of the concerned 
States/Union Territories.  
The important steps taken by Government of India to manage and mitigate 
human-animal conflict in the country include: 
i.  Funds are provided under the National CAMPA for augmentation of 
fodder and water in forest areas for restricting wild animals to forest areas.  An 
amount of Rs. 47,872.31 Crores has been provided to various States for 
promoting afforestation and achieving green objectives of the country during 
2019-2020. 
ii. Ministry provides financial assistance to States/UTs under the Centrally 
Sponsored Schemes of 'Development of Wildlife Habitats', ‘Project Tiger’ and 
‘Project Elephant’ for management of wildlife and its habitats in the country. 
The broad activities supported under these schem es include habitat 
enrichment, water augmentation. 
iii. The funds are also used for construction /erection of physical barriers 
such as solar powered electric fence, bio-fencing using cactus, boundary wall, 
animal proof trenches around forest, etc. 
iv. The financial support to the States/UTs also includes a component of 
compensation due to damage by wild animals. 
v.  Voluntary relocation of villages from the core area of Tiger Reserves, 
National Parks and Sanctuaries are also being funded under the Centrall y 
Sponsored Scheme: ‘Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats’ as proposed 
by the State Governments for avoiding conflict. 
vi. Periodic awareness campaigns to sensitize, guide and advise the 
general public on man -animal conflict, including dissemination  of information 
through various forms of media. 
vii. Directions have been sent to all States/Union Territories for use of 
undergrounding of cables upto 33 KV of electricity cables  in forest areas and 
also maintaining transmission lines to avoid sagging.

Statement 
 
(a)  to (d)   Hon’ble Chief Minister, Government of Andhra Pradesh (GoAP), vide 
letter dated 05.02.2020, has inter -alia requested for intervention of Government of 
India to streamline the procedure for reimbursement of project cost to GoAP in 
respect of Polavaram Irrigation Project (PIP). 
  Government of India has been reimbursing the expenditure on Irrigation 
component of the PIP with effect from 01.04.2014, upon receipt of verified bills and 
recommendations from the Polavaram Project Authority (PPA) and Central Water 
Commission (CWC), with the approval of Ministry of Finance (MoF). 
  Funds are being provided for PIP through Extra Budgetary Resources (EBR) 
from NABARD under Long Term Irrigation Fund (LTIF), after seeking specific approval 
from MoF.   
Further, NABARD raises the funds from the market once requirement of requisite 
amounts is conveyed to them by this Ministry. NABARD normally requires about two 
to three weeks to arrange funds from market (depending upon market conditions) 
and transfer to National Water Development Agency (NWDA). Thereafter, the funds 
are transferred to the GoAP promptly by PPA, normally within one or two working 
days. 
 Response along above lines, was duly conveyed to the Hon’ble CM, GoAP, vide 
letter dated 06
th July 2020.

Statement 
 
(a) Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises is implementing a scheme 
titled ‘Scheme of Fund for Traditional Industries (SFURTI)’.  The main objective of the 
SFURTI scheme is to organize the traditional industries and artisans into clusters, 
including clusters of traditional arts, to make them competitive and provide long term 
sustainable employment.  
Under the scheme, two types of clusters are set up.  The maximum financial 
assistance provided is Rs.2.50 crore for a Regular Cluster (up to 500 artisans) and 
Rs.5.00 crore for a Major Cluster (more than 500 artisans).  The assistance includes 
infrastructure development like setting up of Common Facility Centers, procurement 
of new machineries, raw materials, along with training, exposure visits, etc. 
Till date, 335 clusters have been approved under the scheme and 82 clusters 
are functional. These clusters include sectors like Khadi, Coir, Handloom, Traditional 
Dress Making, Handicraft, Hraditional Arts like – Kalamkari, Dokra art, Bamboo 
products, Food proce ssing including honey, etc.  The list of these clusters is placed 
at Annexure.  
Besides this, Ministry of Textiles implements schemes 
for development of traditional arts under ‘National Handicraft Development 
Programme (NHDP)’ that has 7 components namely (i) Ambedkar Hastshilp Vikas 
Yojana (Base Line Survey & Mobilization of artisans), (ii) Design & Technology Up 
gradation, (iii) Human Resource Development, (iv) Direct Benefit to Artisan, (v) 
Infrastructure and Technology Support, (vi) Research and Develop ment and (vii) 
Marketing Support & Services. In addition, Ministry of Textiles implements 
‘Comprehensive Handicrafts Cluster Development Scheme (CHCDS)’ that has two 
components namely Mega Cluster & Special Projects under Integrated Development 
and Promotion of Handicraft (IDPH). 
Ministry of Tourism under the Swadesh Darshan scheme provides financial 
assistance to the State Govt./UTs/Central Agencies for setting up projects as part of 
development of tourism infrastructure in the country.   Craft Haat/Craft Bazaar, Open 
Air Theatre/Amphi theatres, Souvenir Shops are set up under the scheme to help 
development of traditional arts in the country. 
Ministry of Minority Affairs is implementing a scheme titled  USTTAD  
(Upgrading the Skills and Training in Tradition al Arts/ Crafts for Development) that 
aims at capacity building and upgrading the traditional skills of master 
craftsmen/artisans; training of minority youths in various identified traditional 
arts/crafts; develop national and international market linkages  and preservation of

Union Territories created.  This is not the first time that such a bifurcation has taken

The AGMUT cadre, which is a combined cadre, basically, looks after the Union 
Territories of Delhi, Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram and Goa.  The arrangement, which 
has been made for this cadre, is necessary in order to meet the temporary shortages

created Union Territories, by virtue of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 
2019, seeks to establish this particular cadre in these two Union Territories and merge 
them into the AGMUT cadre so that the management of personnel to meet the 
exigencies arising from time to time in these territories can be met much quickly and in 
a better manner.  The pool of people, who would be available to man positions in 
these two areas in an objective manner, would also increase because of these 
Amendments.   
 The Section 88, of the principal Act, which has been amended, says that the 
members of the Indian Administrative Service, Indian Police Service and the Forest

allocations to these cadres shall also take place similarly.  The objectivity that comes 
into this arrangement because of the reorganisati on is immense in the sense that

larger pool of people who would be selected in the Civil Services examination.
